resources.string: Your app’s map fills the whole cluster. BYD warning lights, ADAS alerts, speed and gear stay displayed on top.
⚠ Test only while stationary: in P with the parking brake applied. The « Back to the BYD display » button stays available at the top of the screen.
On the cluster you should see:
DashCast reads the state of the cluster and of its service without changing anything.
Cannot read the cluster state: the DashCast service does not answer. Reopen DashCast, wait for the connection, then try again.
The connected DashCast service is too old (protocol %1$d required). Close and reopen DashCast to reconnect it, then check again.
This theme is designed for the large 1920 × 720 cluster. A small cluster was detected, so the test is not offered.
Test not possible on this car: DiLink 3 on Android 10 is required. Nothing was sent.
DashCast installs the theme in the cluster. The display does not change yet.
No change: the usual BYD display.
This can take up to a minute. Stay on this page.
Choose the navigation app that will fill the cluster.
The map over the whole cluster, with warning lights, alerts, speed and gear on top.
The map is coming to the cluster.
The cluster received the request. Tell us what you actually see.
Thank you! When you are done, stop the full screen.
Finish the test to return to the BYD display, or start full screen again (%1$s).
The cluster must return to the BYD display before any other step.
An older DashCast test is still loaded. Return to the BYD display first.
The theme has been set aside. A cluster restart completes the return to the BYD display.
A restart was sent but its result is unknown. Do not send it again: check the return to the BYD display.
The cluster screen was not recognised. Return to the BYD display.
An operation is in progress on the cluster.
The cluster state just changed. Wait a moment: the page is updating.
Another operation is in progress. Try again in a moment.
The operation did not complete. Nothing is retried automatically; « Back to the BYD display » stays available. See « Technical details ».
The car is stationary, in P, with the parking brake applied.
This is the cluster intended for this test (DashCast checks its exact version before any change).
I am restoring the original BYD display on this vehicle.
DashCast copies the theme to the cluster and selects it.
The display stays the BYD one at this step.
The « Back to the BYD display » button stays available at all times.
The cluster switches to projection mode.
%1$s is shown over the whole cluster.
You can stop it at any time from this page.
The theme stays loaded: you can start again or finish the test.
The usual BYD display comes back.
What do you see on the cluster?
The map fills the cluster, with warning lights, speed and gear
Nothing changed: the usual BYD display
Black screen, « Simple mode » or abnormal display
Wait a few seconds, then look again. If nothing changes, stop the full screen.
No DashCast theme is loaded. Just check that the cluster shows the usual BYD screen.
The cluster refused the return and keeps the DashCast theme. Set the theme aside: DashCast will then guide you to restart the cluster.
The theme has been set aside. Press « Back to the BYD display » to continue: a cluster restart will be offered.
DashCast requests the original BYD display again.
If needed, a cluster restart will be offered next.
DashCast closes the temporary BYD projection; no theme had been selected.
The usual BYD display, with its warning lights and instruments.
DashCast moves its test theme; the file is kept.
No change on the cluster yet.
Check the return to the BYD display?
DashCast checks that the original BYD display is selected. Nothing is retried.
DashCast opens and closes the BYD projection once to apply the original profile.
DashCast checks again that its theme has been set aside.
The cluster and screens restart; ADB is interrupted for a moment.
After the restart: the usual BYD display.
DashCast asks the cluster to leave the BYD projection mode.
Look at the cluster: do you see the usual BYD display with its warning lights and instruments? Answer only after looking.
